instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: Half a season, but the half that produced four at Anfield and followed a Euro 2008 in which he was among the best players in the tournament.
Back in the side after the knee operations — short of 1987 but still world class.
A Ballon d’Or winner at 32 playing sweeper and midfield; the output is small, the football was elite.
Player-manager who barely selected himself; declining, but still the best technician on the pitch when he played.
Two years on from the United bench he was a first-choice centre-back for a treble-winning Barcelona and months from a World Cup.
Back after eighteen months lost to a knee injury and never quite the same runner; the passing and the movement survived it.
An expensive teenage prospect at Liverpool, but raw and used sparingly; rated as the player he was, not the Man City regular he became.
An ever-present in a treble-winning side, scoring in the UEFA Cup final, a year after a Champions League final with Bayern; a Germany first choice at his peak.
Guillain-Barré syndrome cost him effectively two years; back playing at thirty but never the same athlete, which is why this sits eight points below 2000/01.
Twenty-three and already Italy’s left-back, but not yet the player of his mid-nineties peak.
Thirty-five and still the best defender in the side; a rung below his own peak but plainly elite.
Relegated, but the left foot was the best thing at the club: the delivery was already of a standard above the side around him.
A January move from a relegated side to City and an immediate step up: five assists in half a season and an England call-up on the strength of it.
Southampton’s player of the season in an FA Cup final year; a Sweden international and the most reliable defender at the club.
Twenty and a regular in the back four through the record run of fourteen straight clean sheets; a clear step up on the loan season.
Four goals and seven assists from right-back in a side that won the league with 81 points; one of the best attacking full-backs in Europe that season.
Lost his place to Tim Flowers in November.
Twenty-seven league goals at twenty-one in a side built around Cristiano Ronaldo; elite movement and finishing, not yet the complete centre-forward.
His one season as an undisputed first choice, and good enough in a relegated side to earn a Manchester United move as understudy.
Captain of a treble-winning side and eleven league assists from full-back; the best right-back in the world at this point.
Twenty-four league goals, the Scudetto and the Ballon d’Or at the end of that calendar year; world class, and eleven points above the broken-down twenty-nine-year-old at Chelsea.
Rated well below the Milan forward who won a Ballon d’Or: at twenty-nine the pace had gone and a back problem had taken much of the rest, and four league goals in twenty-two starts is what was left.
Moved from Lazio to Inter in January; the same footballer at both clubs.
Moved from Lazio to Inter in January; the same footballer at both clubs.
Signed from Atletico Madrid and a capable squad player for the champions at 22; the minutes reflect the competition ahead of him, not his level.
Lost the left-back place over the course of the relegation season; the pace and the crossing were already going at twenty-eight.
Twelve goals and an England cap at twenty-two; the ability was briefly genuine, which the following two seasons do not reflect.
The season was ended in October by a broken leg. Rated as the France international and twice Ligue 1 top scorer he was at twenty-two: frightening pace and a real finish, raw everywhere else.
Twenty-four, and already the deep playmaker the whole side was built around; world class a decade before the Juventus row.
A European Cup winner and man of the match in the final; at twenty-seven he was one of the three or four best midfielders in the world.
Twenty-one, fourteen starts and a substitute in the European Cup final; the ball retention was already there, the influence was not yet.
Thirty and injury-interrupted, captaining a treble side; down from the 2009/10 peak but still a genuinely elite midfielder.
